post.description:
Reserve an avatar and return the WebRTC details your client needs to join it.

Address the avatar directly with `persona_id` or `persona_slug`, or pass an `agent_id` to start from a stored agent. Agent sessions take the avatar and voice agent configuration from the agent, and the response additionally carries `voice_agent_details`: short-lived, browser-safe credentials for the agent's voice provider, so the vendor key never leaves Keyframe.

Agent sessions also accept `overrides` (per-session changes the agent has allowed) and `dynamic_variables` (values for `{{placeholders}}` in the system prompt and greeting). Both are validated before any capacity is reserved.

get.description:
Agents in your organization, newest first. Drafts are omitted; fetch one by ID to read a draft.

Agents are designed and published on the Keyframe platform. This API reads them and starts sessions from them; it does not create or edit them.

post.description:
Mint a short-lived token that lets a browser start one session with this agent without ever seeing your API key.

This is how `private` agents are used from a client: call this endpoint from your backend, relay the `token` to the page, and pass it to the client SDK as `conversationToken` in place of an `agent_id`. The agent's origin allowlist is not applied to token sessions, since your backend has already authorized the caller. Public agents accept tokens too.

Use `dynamic_variables` to bind per-user values (a name, an account tier) into the token. They take precedence over anything the client sends when it exchanges the token.

post.description:
Returns a signed URL to PUT one audio file to. Takes no request body. Upload the raw bytes with no required headers, then pass the returned `id` as `audio_file_id`.

One upload can back several generations -- the same audio rendered as mp4 and webm, or re-run with a different emotion timeline -- without re-sending it.

post.description:
Queues a batch render and returns immediately with a `queued` job. Poll it, or supply a `webhook`.

The uploaded audio is inspected before the job is created: an unreadable file, a file containing a video stream, an unsupported codec or one longer than the limit is rejected with 400 and nothing is queued. `duration_seconds` in the response is measured, not declared.

RecallApiKeyHeader.name: Recall-Api-Key
RecallApiKeyHeader.description: Recall AI API key used to spawn and manage the bot

AgentIdPath.name: agent_id
AgentIdPath.description: The agent's public `agent_...` handle. The internal UUID is accepted too.

agent_id.description: Agent to start the session from (see GET /agents). The agent supplies the avatar and voice agent configuration, and the response includes `voice_agent_details`. The agent must be `active`.

participant_token.description: JWT for 'source' participant to pass audio to avatar

agent_identity.description: Identity of the avatar in the WebRTC session

voice_agent_details.description: Browser-side credentials for the agent's voice provider. Set only for sessions created with `agent_id`; `null` otherwise.

Agent.description: An avatar paired with a voice agent configuration, designed and published on the Keyframe platform. Sessions started from an agent inherit its configuration.

id.description: Internal identifier. Use `agent_id` in API calls and client code.

agent_id.description: Public handle: `agent_` followed by 32 hex characters. Immutable, and safe to ship in client code for `public` agents.

label.description: Display name set on the platform.

status.description: Only `active` agents can start sessions. `GET /agents` omits drafts.

auth.description: `public`: a page on an allowed origin can start a session with the bare `agent_id`. `private`: client sessions require a conversation token minted server-side with POST /agents/{agent_id}/token.

allowed_overrides.description: Fields a caller may change per session via `overrides`. Anything else is rejected with 403.

dynamic_variable_defaults.description: Fallback values for `{{placeholders}}` in the system prompt and greeting. Values supplied at session or token creation take precedence.

allowed_origins.description: Browser origins that may start sessions with the bare `agent_id`. Not applied to sessions started with a conversation token or an API key.

publishable_key.description: Legacy `kfl_pk_live_...` handle, present only on agents created before agent IDs. Use `agent_id` instead.

source_config_id.description: For an edit draft, the published agent it was forked from.

AgentSessionOverrides.description: Per-session changes to a Keyframe Voice Agent's configuration. Every field you send must appear in the agent's `allowed_overrides`, or the request fails with 403 before any capacity is reserved. Only agents whose `voice_agent.type` is `kfl` accept overrides.

system_prompt.description: May contain `{{placeholders}}`; they are filled from `dynamic_variables`.

greeting.description: First message the agent speaks. An empty string disables it so the agent waits for the user.

voice_id.description: An active voice from GET /voices. The TTS provider, model and voice settings follow the new voice.

DynamicVariables.description: Values for `{{placeholders}}` in the agent's system prompt and greeting. Names use letters, digits and underscores (up to 100 characters); names starting with `system__` are reserved. Values are strings up to 2000 characters; numbers and booleans are converted to strings. At most 40 entries. A placeholder left without a value fails the request with 400.

KflVoiceAgent.title: Keyframe Voice Agent
KflVoiceAgent.description: Keyframe's first-party voice agent: speech-to-text, an LLM, and text-to-speech run by Keyframe. The only type that supports `overrides` and dynamic variables.

tts_model.description: Text-to-speech model; the provider's default when null.

stt_model.description: Speech-to-text model; the provider's default when null.

system_prompt.description: May contain `{{placeholders}}` filled from dynamic variables.

greeting.default: Hello! How can I help you today?
greeting.description: First message the agent speaks. An empty string means no first message; the agent waits for the user. May contain `{{placeholders}}`.

first_message_interruptible.description: Whether the user can talk over the greeting. When false the greeting always plays to the end.

ws_auth_ttl_seconds.description: How long the `signed_url` in `voice_agent_details` stays valid before the client must connect.

stt_max_endpoint_delay_ms.description: Maximum end-of-utterance delay (ms) for the speech-to-text endpointer

voice_settings.description: Provider-specific synthesis settings; see `voice_settings` on GET /voices for the voice's defaults.

tools.description: Tools the LLM may call. `set_emotion` lets it change the avatar's expression mid-conversation.

agent_id.description: Agent ID from the ElevenLabs dashboard.

turn_detection.description: OpenAI Realtime `turn_detection` configuration, passed through as-is.

ttl_seconds.description: How long the token can be exchanged for a session. Does not limit the session's own duration.

dynamic_variables.description: Bound into the token. These win over values the client passes when exchanging the token, so your backend controls what the browser cannot change.

token.description: Opaque conversation token. Relay it to the browser; the client SDK exchanges it for a session.

expires_at.description: Unix time (seconds) after which the token can no longer be exchanged.

VoiceAgentDetails.description: Short-lived, browser-safe credentials for the agent's voice provider, discriminated by `type`. Never contains the vendor API key.

signed_url.description: Signed WebSocket URL for the Keyframe voice agent runtime. Any overrides and rendered dynamic variables are bound into the signature, so the client cannot alter them.

ApiErrorResponse.description: Structured error envelope used by the Generations and Uploads endpoints. A superset of the `detail` shape the older endpoints return: `code` is stable and safe to branch on, `param` names the offending field when one is identifiable.

param.description: Request field that caused the error, when known.

CreateUploadResponse.description: A signed URL for one audio upload. Takes no request body: anything you could declare here would be unverified, so size and content are checked against the stored object when the generation is created.

id.description: Pass as `audio_file_id` when creating a generation.

upload_url.description: PUT the raw audio bytes here. No headers are required.

expires_at.description: After this the URL stops working, but the id stays valid for an upload already completed.

at.description: Seconds from the start of the clip. Floored to the model's one-second inference window.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint that receives lifecycle events.

secret.description: Signs deliveries as `KFL-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hmac-sha256>` over `"{t}.{body}"`. Generated if omitted.

CreateGenerationRequest.description: Queue a batch video generation. The audio must already be uploaded via POST /uploads.

model.description: Must appear in your plan's allowed models.

audio_file_id.description: `id` returned by POST /uploads, after the audio has been PUT to the signed URL.

emotion.description: One emotion for the whole clip, or a timeline. Resolution is one second.

metadata.description: Returned unchanged on reads and webhooks; never interpreted.

status.description: Terminal states are `done` and `failed`. There is no cancelled state.

duration_seconds.description: Measured from the uploaded audio, not supplied by the caller.

credits_estimated.description: Quote at submit. The charge is based on what is actually rendered.

output_url.description: Signed download link, valid 30 minutes. Re-read the generation for a fresh one; it is not stored.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `after` for the next page. Opaque.
